question: v07
q: Where is the RBA at with rates?

transcript.answer:
The RBA cash rate target was **4.35%** as of the latest data (September 2026). That's after a run of hikes in the first half of 2026, which undid the 2025 easing cycle.

**How it got there (monthly average cash rate target, RBA table F1.1):**

| Period | Rate | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| Up to Jan 2025 | 4.35% | Peak of the 2022–23 hiking cycle |
| Feb–Sep 2025 | Fell to 3.60% | Four cuts of 25 basis points (Feb, May, Aug 2025, plus one in Mar–Apr shown by the averages) |
| Sep 2025 – Jan 2026 | 3.60% | On hold |
| Feb–May 2026 | Rose to 4.35% | Three hikes of 25 basis points, in about early Feb, mid-Mar and early May (dates estimated from the monthly averages) |
| Jun–Sep 2026 | 4.35% | On hold |

So the rate is back at the 2023–24 peak. All of the 2025 easing has been reversed.

**One thing to check:** September's average was 4.36%, not 4.35%. That small difference could mean the target changed in the last day or so of the month, possibly at a late-September meeting. I couldn't get daily figures to confirm it, so check the RBA's latest decision before relying on 4.35%.

**Why they've been hiking:** inflation has picked up again and is above the RBA's 2–3% target band.
- **Headline CPI:** 4.0% year-on-year in August 2026, up from 3.5% in July and as high as 4.6% in March.
- **Trimmed mean** (the RBA's preferred underlying measure): 3.6% in August 2026, up steadily from 3.3% in January. This rise in underlying inflation is the main reason for the hikes.

With underlying inflation still climbing, the data point to the RBA staying firm rather than cutting any time soon.
